caseStudyHeader.heading: Self-service portal
caseStudyHeader.body: A cross-device self-service experience, shaped by administrator settings for an IAM platform.

summary.title: Outcome
summary.description: The platform now has a self-service experience aligned with its capabilities and supports complex configuration without compromising usability.

summary.title: Goal
summary.description: The capability needed to be configurable, brandable, and balance consumer-grade usability with enterprise requirements.

summary.title: Role
summary.description: I led the design for the Self-Service experience and two upstream application areas that it relied on.

summary.title: Client and scope
summary.description: The internal client for this project was Thales’ Identity and Access Management (IAM) organization. The engagement intermittently across 11 months in 2025.

context.statement: How might we design a better way for admins to configure a self-service experience?
list: IAM platforms perform many functions and Self-service is a foundational element.
Out-of-the-box self-service experiences are often limited in functionality and lag in usability.
Customers tend to build their own, but are left with the burden of maintaining them.
The vision was to make the self-service experience highly configurable and consumer grade.

subsections.subhead: Admins can configure experiences to meet their organization’s security needs

showcases.captionBody: Admins define which attributes appear on a user's profile and how users can interact with them.

images.alt: Self-service settings in the admin console: a table of profile attributes with toggles for whether each is visible and required, and its mutability.

showcases.captionBody: End users, such as employees and customers, experience the results of an admin's profile configuration choices.

images.alt: The end user's Personal information page, showing the profile fields the admin chose to make visible and editable.

subsections.subhead: Admins customize and end users receive a branded cross-device experience

images.alt: Unbranded Email addresses page on desktop, with the platform's default styling.
The same unbranded Email addresses page on a phone.

showcases.captionBody: Token-based theming provides impactful branding while keeping admin configuration minimal.

images.alt: The Email addresses page on desktop with a customer's brand applied: logo, header color and button color.
The same branded Email addresses page on a phone.

subsections.subhead: End users navigate standardized security workflows

showcases.captionTitle: End user last passkey removal flow
showcases.captionBody: This flow is based on the FIDO alliance’s standard and adapted for our platform.

images.alt: Three steps of removing a last passkey: the passkey list, the warning that removing it leaves no sign-in method, and the confirmation screen.

process.statement: The most complex challenge was to design a configurable user profile.
process.description: This was complex because flexible profile configuration had to comply with SCIM 2.0 requirements while also integrating with legacy platform components.

outcomes.quote: In a space where scope was poorly defined across four product areas, Scott delivered a coherent solution through close collaboration with PM, architecture, and engineering.
list: Self-Service was a dormant capability with unclear requirements and dependencies
I drove commitment and delivered a flexible, usable self-service experience
I extended theming, enabled full branded experiences across the platform
I introduced workflows and components for our platform’s growing complexity
